title: Runtime Cost & Latency Auditor — per-route / per-model / tenant slicing service
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a scalable service that converts raw runtime telemetry (per-request spans, kernel timings, KV cache events, batching metadata) into explainable per-route, per-model, and per-tenant cost and latency breakdowns for the Console and billing analytics. This service (LatCost Auditor) must produce both near-real-time rollups for the Console (1-5 min latency) and daily authoritative rollups for billing reconciliation.

Inputs: streaming telemetry from inference runtime (Kafka topic: runtime.telemetry.v2) that includes: request metadata (route ID, tenant ID, model version), timing spans (enqueue, dispatch, kernel-run, postprocess), token counts, batch sizes, cache hit/miss events, GPU kernel microtimings, and network egress/ingress latencies. Also accepts model pricing profiles and per-tenant overrides from config service.

Outputs: materialized per-route/per-model/per-tenant breakdowns with components: token compute cost, kernel time fraction, batching overhead, KV-cache delta, queuing+network overhead, and an internal reconciliation score (confidence). Outputs are written to ClickHouse for fast Console queries and daily canonical records to the ledger S3 prefix for billing.

Key challenges / decisions: 1) attribution model: we will attribute cost primarily at the token level but adjust for batching economies (amortize shared kernel time across contributing requests using weighted token share). For KV cache hits waveform we deduct cached token compute; for fallback model substitutions we tag the request and emit both requested and served model entries for transparency. 2) Sampling vs full-fidelity: initial design processes 100% of events for 1-50K tenants, then uses adaptive reservoir sampling for bulk tenants to bound pipeline cost. 3) Streaming correctness: use exactly-once semantics in the Flink processor (stateful windowing keyed by (tenant, route, model)) with idempotent writes to ClickHouse via upsert keys. 4) Privacy/compliance: tenant PII is never materialized; tenant IDs are hashed prior to long-term storage for compliance when requested by security.

Operational goals: end-to-end latency <= 5m for Console slices, daily canonical ledger accuracy within 0.5% of runtime cost reports, and pipeline resource cost target < 0.25% of total inference spend.

This ticket scopes the service scaffold, telemetry schema contract, core Flink pipeline implementation, ClickHouse schema, and the daily densifier job that reconciles streaming aggregates into canonical ledgers.
acceptance_criteria: Schema contract documented and consumed by runtime team (link in comments)
Flink pipeline prototype processes synthetic traffic at 10k RPS with correct per-route attribution in staging
ClickHouse materialized views expose per-route, per-model, per-tenant breakdowns with query < 1s for 30d window in staging
Daily ledger export job produces canonical S3 files matching table-of-records format and a reconciliation report
End-to-end Console dashboard shows near-real-time slices (1-5m) for three sample tenants
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff with Runtime and Billing: agreed payload fields and stable topic name runtime.telemetry.v2. Action: runtime to add kernel microtimings and batch contributor list. (Confluence spec link in links)

2026-02-24 - Design review: choose Flink over Beam because of our team's operational familiarity and stateful window support. Decided on keyed-window by (tenant, route, model) with 1m tumbling windows and retrospective correction using event-time processing.

2026-03-02 - Prototype complete: local Flink job ingests mocked telemetry and emits per-window attribution. Found an edge case where multi-tenant batching across routes skews attribution; added correction where shared batch time is split by token-weighted origin flags.
2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff: security requested hashing of tenant IDs for long-term storage and an access-control checklist for ClickHouse tables. Marked security_review_required = true.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 contains Flink job implementation and ClickHouse DDL. Needs two reviewers from infra and billing.
2026-03-11 - Load test in staging: 12k RPS, median processing latency 1.2m, occasional spikes due to GC in a single operator. Next: add JVM tuning and operator parallelism changes.
